title: Ei ole with plural owners
focus: Use fixed ei ole with meillä, teillä, and heillä when possession is denied.

exercises.prompt: Choose “You do not have a book.” in Finnish. Use teillä (“you as the owner”) and kirjaa (“a book”). Frame: “Teillä ___ kirjaa”. Address a group.
exercises.explanation: The owner phrase names the owner. Negative possession keeps fixed ei ole; it does not conjugate the negative verb to match the owner.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Fixed ei ole in possession: form or meaning confused

The owner phrase names the owner. Negative possession keeps fixed ei ole; it does not conjugate the negative verb to match the owner.

sentenceExplanation.translation: You do not have a book.
sentenceExplanation.pattern: possessor + fixed ei ole + singular partitive noun

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: te has the learned possession form teillä; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Possession uses fixed ei with meillä, teillä and heillä; do not change it to emme, ette or eivät.
After ei, olla uses ole. Together ei ole means “do not have” or “does not have” here.
kirja + -a = kirjaa. This is the singular partitive, the noun form used when possession is denied.

answerDiagnostics.category: Fixed ei ole in possession: predictable form error
answerDiagnostics.explanation: The -lla/-llä phrase is the possessor. In this possession pattern the verb stays fixed, so do not conjugate it to match the owner.
